purpose: Verify AR Credit Memo schema, permission seeding, currency rounding and remaining credit amounts, invoice void protection, concurrent confirmations, idempotent commands, credit applications and the shared refund balance contract.
data: Two MySQL schema checks verify permission seeds and credit/refund constraints in a freshly migrated private schema. Two HTTP cases use synthetic customers and a single opening invoice or a single shipped two-line order, with one matching posted return for source validation. Three in-memory tests cover per-line caps and shared credit balance locking. The added TC-020 regression uses one in-memory stub returning an absent-schema row with no credit table count; it writes no database rows.
concurrency: Existing routine server jobs and shard configuration. The HTTP case uses two concurrent confirmations for one original invoice to verify serialized credit limits. No new worker or job.
repetitions: Eight added functional cases run once per applicable existing routine server run. The three refreshed TC-020 fixtures keep their existing execution counts. Browser tests remain explicit local evidence and are outside this candidate.
thresholds: Exact money and schema constraints; permissions, idempotency and transactional outcomes match the assertions. Existing thresholds and coverage floors are preserved.
trigger: Existing server functional discovery only. No workflow, schedule, capacity or performance changes.
cost: Author measured the two HTTP cases together at 5.3 seconds in UTC and 7.3 seconds in Asia/Hong_Kong per timezone including setup; the other five cases total under one second locally. The added TC-020 in-memory case took under 1 ms locally. Remote CI critical-path impact is unmeasured.
